world.description: a pencil logistics and supply network

world.label: Pencil Logistics Network
world.summary: Specialists turn recurring orders and raw materials into pencils that reach a shop's customers.

actions.description: Harvest logs from the forest for the lumber mill.
Saw logs into boards for the pencil slat maker.
Cut boards into pencil slats for the pencil assembler.
Collect graphite from the deposit for the pencil assembler.
Assemble pencils from slats and graphite for the shopkeeper.
Place a recurring pencil order with the shopkeeper.
Sell one pencil from the shopkeeper's stock to a customer.

mechanics.rationale: The logger harvests available logs and delivers them to the named mill worker.

checks.label: The logger is working as a logger
The forest has logs available
The named forest is the forest being harvested
The named mill is the mill receiving the logs

limits: Harvests one log per action; does not represent travel, tools, or mill capacity.
tests: A logger harvesting from a forest with logs transfers one log to the named mill worker.
Refuse when the source has no logs or either action reference does not match its participant.
semantic_bindings: forest logs are the harvested raw material
mill logs are the delivered material

mechanics.rationale: The mill worker uses one log to make one board and delivers that board to the named slat maker.

checks.label: The worker is working at the lumber mill
The mill worker has a log to saw
The named slat maker is receiving the boards

limits: Consumes one log and delivers one board per action; does not model waste or mill capacity.
tests: With a log available, the mill worker consumes one log and gives one board to the named slat maker.
Refuse if the actor has no log or the action reference does not match the slat maker.
semantic_bindings: actor logs are the sawing input
slat maker boards are the delivered output

mechanics.rationale: The slat maker uses one board to make one slat and delivers it to the named assembler.

checks.label: The worker is working as a slat maker
The slat maker has a board to cut
The named assembler is receiving the slat

limits: Consumes one board and delivers one slat per action; does not model cutting waste or capacity.
tests: With a board available, the slat maker consumes one board and gives one slat to the named assembler.
Refuse if the actor has no board or the action reference does not match the assembler.
semantic_bindings: actor boards are the cutting input
assembler slats are the delivered output

mechanics.rationale: The miner collects one available unit of graphite and delivers it to the named assembler.

checks.label: The worker is working as a graphite miner
The deposit has graphite available
The named deposit is the source being mined
The named assembler is receiving the graphite

limits: Collects and delivers one graphite unit per action; does not model mining equipment or capacity.
tests: With graphite available, mining removes one unit from the deposit and gives it to the named assembler.
Refuse if the deposit is empty or either action reference does not match its participant.
semantic_bindings: deposit graphite is the mined raw material
assembler graphite is the delivered material

mechanics.rationale: The assembler consumes one slat and one graphite unit to make one pencil and delivers it to the named shopkeeper.

checks.label: The worker is working as a pencil assembler
The assembler has a slat
The assembler has graphite
The named shopkeeper is receiving the pencil

limits: Consumes one slat and one graphite unit and delivers one pencil per action; does not model other materials or production capacity.
tests: With both inputs available, the assembler consumes one of each and delivers a pencil to the named shopkeeper.
Refuse when either input is missing or the action reference does not match the shopkeeper.
semantic_bindings: assembler slats and graphite are pencil inputs
shopkeeper pencils are the delivered finished product

mechanics.rationale: The shopkeeper records a recurring pencil order in the represented order inventory.

checks.label: The worker is the pencil shopkeeper
The order is being placed with this shopkeeper

limits: Records one order per action; the represented state does not specify order size, payment, or fulfillment rules.
tests: A shopkeeper placing an order increases the shopkeeper's order count by one.
Refuse when the actor is not a shopkeeper or the action reference is not that shopkeeper.
semantic_bindings: shopkeeper orders represent recorded pencil demand

mechanics.rationale: The shopkeeper transfers one stocked pencil to the named customer.

checks.label: The worker is the pencil shopkeeper
The shopkeeper has a pencil in stock
The named customer is receiving the pencil

limits: Transfers one pencil per action; the represented state does not include payment or customer ownership.
tests: With a pencil in stock, the shopkeeper transfers one pencil to the named customer.
Refuse when stock is empty or the action reference does not match the customer.

processes.rationale: The forest regrows logs and the deposit replenishes graphite, renewing the represented raw-material sources each round.
Customer demand continues to arrive each round as represented orders.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The graphite-miner and logger supplied inputs, the lumber-mill made boards, the slat-maker cut slats, and the pencil-assembler made pencils for the shopkeeper. The records show goods moving between production steps, but do not show pencils reaching customers or a production step waiting for missing supplies.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: The lumber-mill used logs to make boards, the slat-maker used boards to cut slats, and the pencil-assembler used graphite and slats to make pencils.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: The graphite-miner and logger moved inputs to the pencil-assembler and lumber-mill; boards and slats then moved to the next producers, and pencils went to the shopkeeper.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.missing_reason: No finished goods are shown reaching and being taken or used by the place that wants them.

mechanisms.name: Work held up
mechanisms.missing_reason: No event shows a step unable to proceed because needed goods had not arrived or had run out.
